Calvin Coolidge, without a doubt.
Much like Reagan would do six decades later, Coolidge used the bully pulpit to change the perception of how government should work.
In an era of big government tax-and-spend Presidents like Teddy Roosevelt, Woodrow Wilson, Herbert Hoover and FDR, Coolidge stood apart.
He cut taxes substantially on at least three occasions and appointed laissez-faire businessmen to government agencies like the Federal Trade Commission and Interstate Commerce Commission.
The federal debt was reduced by one-fourth as state and local governments grew substantially and surpassed the federal budget.
Coolidge also vetoed farm subsidies, disdained federal intervention in flood control, spoke in favor of civil rights for blacks and Catholics and was wary of foreign entanglements.

As a libertarian, what is your ranking of the 5 best and 5 worst US presidents?

Combining notes from libertarians Ivan Eland (author of Recarving Rushmore) and Brion McClanahan (author of 9 President who screwed up America and 4 who tried to save her) you get a list looking like this (most lists I have found seem to have a relative consensus on the first four in both constitutionality and policy).

Combining notes from libertarians Ivan Eland (author of Recarving Rushmore) and Brion McClanahan (author of 9 President who screwed up America and 4 who tried to save her) you get a list looking like this (most lists I have found seem to have a relative consensus on the first four in both constitutionality and policy).
John Tyler: ranked as number 1 by both.
Firm believer in states rights.
Continually vetoed unconstitutional legislation.
Avoided war with the British.
Fought against the banks.

Overall the historians have largely ranked him one of the worst due to the fact that he wasn’t an authoritarian war-monger and that he wasn’t harsh on slavery (he owned slaves himself and thought Liberia was a possible solution).
Grover Cleveland: according to BM he was the last true conservative President.
He was super anti-corruption, helped set our monetary policy in order, and was very anti-imperialistic.
He was also Ron Paul’s favorite President.

Martin Van Buren: according to IE allowed the market to readjust fairly quickly after the Panic of 1837, reduced public spending, balanced the budget, and avoided potential wars with Canada and Mexico.
Calvin Coolidge: the last true President we ever had.
He understood that the American Presidency really shouldn’t have all that much effect over an average person’s daily life.

The more I read about him from his avoiding war with Mexico, to helping lower lynchings of African Americans, and to being one of the only Presidents who actually weakened the power of the Presidency, it’s hard to conclude this guy wasn’t the one of the best we ever had if not the best.
Franklin Pierce: while given far too much blame for the Kansas Nebraska act, this has caused people to overlook the immense good he did.
He had one of the least corrupt cabinets of any President, demolished the debt by over 80%, avoided war with Britain, and continully vetoed unconstitutional legislation.
Another top contender I’d say is Zachary Taylor with many lists having him ranked much higher than the Virginian DRs and is also considered one of the more constitutional Presidents by BM.
However his Presidency was fairly short and his accomplishments were arguably not as lasting as the Virginia DRs.
James Monroe was also excellent and the most Jeffersonian of the Virginia dynast.
Republicans Grant, Hayes, Arthur, and Harding are also worth considering even if they didn’t have the staunch constitutionality the other aforementioned Presidents had.

Woodrow Wilson: authoritarian war-monger who got us the Federal reserve, introduced the national income tax, brought about multiple recessions, and started the rhetoric that viewed the constitution as an enemy of progress.
Harry Truman: again an authoritarian war-monger who specifically said we were going to put international principles over American principles.

To give him a little credit he was more or less following the path laid out by FDR but he nonetheless put America in a continual state of “being at war” that has existed to this day and even attempts at restrained foreign policy from Eisenhower, Carter, and Trump haven’t been enough to stop that.
Abraham Lincoln: while ending slavery was indeed good, his actions for getting us to that point set a bad precedent of authoritarian power that Presidents since have followed.
LBJ: unconstitutional war on poverty, wars in Vietnam and Laos, created the welfare state, and undid JFK’s work to get rid of the Federal Reserve before his body was even cold.
FDR: attempted to pack the courts, expanded spending in a massive way, and lead us down the path we are today of being the world police (although Truman was the one who continued it).
Other top contenders are Bush Senior, Clinton, Bush Junior, and Obama.
All were unconstitutional and each was more unconstitutional than the last, all got us into wars, and all expanded the power of the executive.
